data.body:
WHAT: ONE data table keyed by model family (claude, openai, gemini, deepseek, kimi, qwen, glm, unknown): cache kind (explicit|automatic|none), ttl options, read/write multipliers, min cacheable tokens, window, compaction kind, each fact a three-valued record (status, source, date) in the HX-facts-core shape; plus per-harness capabilities the advisor needs (can run a compaction command, which hooks accept additionalContext, usage fields in transcripts, ttl env). Run and record the probes listed in research section 11 (hooks that reach subagents, PostCompact fields, PreCompact fields, Kimi/Codex caching). REUSE: HX-facts-core (fact shape), B-am-harness-probe ([transcripts] stays there), SU-client-table (client capabilities), research/mcp-client-matrix.md. Do not edit harnesses/*.toml. WHY: model family differs from harness (Claude Code can run non-Claude models); prices move so they are dated data, never code. TEST: every harness id has a row or an explicit unknown; every fact has source and date; a fact older than [context].facts_max_age_days makes doctor note it; unverified is never read as true. ACCEPTANCE: probe record per UNVERIFIED line of research section 11.

ADDED by D-TE-Q2: include the per-agent compact-window knob table from TE-compact-window-per-agent.

Scope note (impl-cc-inventory): globs widened to the harness-capability file, the loader and the [context] section module. Wiring the section into config.py and the doctor note into api/reporting/health.py overlaps live leases (impl-governor-core, impl-review-finding): filed as follow-up CC-inventory-wire.

services/context_families.py has doctor_notes(max_age_days) and DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_DAYS=90. Add the [context] section (facts_max_age_days, four ways, knob docs), register it in config.py, and append CF.doctor_notes(cfg.context.facts_max_age_days) to doctor notes. Filed by CC-inventory because config.py and health.py were under live leases (impl-governor-core, impl-review-finding). Test: a stale fact appears in doctor output; golden snapshots, README knob table and pins regenerated.
data.title: Wire context facts: [context].facts_max_age_days knob in config.py and the doctor note in api/reporting/health.py

data.claim: PostCompact carries compact_summary; PreCompact carries custom_instructions; settings hooks fire in subagents with agent_id

Docs read, not executed; delivery of additionalContext to a subagent's model stays open (context-probes.md row 1).

Probe + regression test test_a_malformed_or_misspelt_fact_is_not_silently_dropped; mutation (disabling the not-a-fact check) makes it fail (1 failed, 10 passed), restored passes; fixed in 9034a812/e1acb3c32. Harness-id test asserts IDS is non-empty (no vacuous pass).

Searched by operation: TOML loading (infra/tomlcfg is a dataclass-overlay loader, not applicable), fact/status shapes (no other implementation; HX-facts-core unbuilt, same {status,source,date} fields), date parsing (uses core.clock.parse_date, ratchet-enforced), family names (config_sections/agent.FAMILY_HINTS maps model substrings to vendor, a different job; DRV-model-catalog will make it a reader). roborev duplicate check clean.

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` is still not robust to malformed shipped data: it assumes the `unknown` family row is a mapping before checking that it has no facts. Given `validate({"context_families.toml": {"family": {"unknown": "x"}}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}})`, `_shape_problems` correctly reports that `family.unknown` is not a table, but execution then reaches `elif any(is_fact(v) for v in family_row(data, UNKNOWN).values())`. `family_row(data, "unknown")` returns the string `"x"`, so `.values()` raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'values'` instead of returning the malformed-data problem. The same class of crash exists in `_shape_problems` for a non-table top-level table such as `{"context_families.toml": {"family": "x"}, ...}`. This is not fully answered by the previous fix to `facts`, which only skips non-table rows.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: The `exc` override path can silently override every model when the table contains an empty key, because `usable` treats an empty string as a substring of any non-empty model name. `_shape_problems` accepts any known field named `exc` without checking that its keys are non-empty model substrings, so a fact such as `{"s": "verified", "v": "explicit", "src": "x", "d": "2024-01-01", "exc": {"": "automatic"}}` can pass validation (with `x` present in `[sources]`), but `usable(fact, "gpt")` returns `"automatic"` for every non-empty model. That is wrong because the family value `v` is the global value; an empty `exc` key is not a model name and should not match.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:usable

chunk_findings.detail: The acceptance criterion requires a probe record for each UNVERIFIED line from research section 11, including hooks that reach subagents, PostCompact summary, Kimi cache, and compaction-cold cache write. The new research file still contains a “Not done, on purpose” section, and the earlier finding that the required probes are not executed remains unanswered: the UNVERIFIED lines are backed only by page reads, not by executed probe records on this machine as the file’s own `verified` definition requires.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:"Not done, on purpose"

chunk_findings.detail: The `claude` row encodes `min_tokens.v = 512` and `window.v = 1000000` as family-wide `documented` facts, but the facts’ own notes say older Claude models differ (`1024-4096` minimum tokens, `200K` window) and no `exc` entries encode those differences. Given a model such as `claude-3-5-sonnet`, the loader/advisor reads `min_tokens = 512` and `window = 1000000` with status `documented`; the advisor can attempt cache writes below the provider minimum and can overestimate the usable context window by 5x. The file’s contract says `exc` is for models that differ from `v`, so these documented model-family differences are not actually represented in the machine-readable data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:37-38

chunk_findings.detail: The `openai` row’s `ttl` and `write_mult` facts are marked `documented` for the whole family, but their notes restrict them to GPT-5.6+ and say GPT-5.5 is “24h only” and earlier models have no write fee. Given `gpt-5.5`, `ttl` returns `["30m", "12h"]` and `write_mult` returns `{30m: 1.25, 12h: 2.5}` with status `documented`, while the row itself says the correct TTL is 24h and earlier models have no separate cache-write multiplier. This makes the advisor use wrong cache TTL options and wrong cache-write cost for OpenAI models that are not GPT-5.6+.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:43-45

chunk_findings.detail: `kimi.window` is `documented` with `v = 1048576`, but the note says that is the K3 series and that the K2 series is `262144`. Given a K2 model such as `kimi-k2-0711-preview`—which the file says is not closed to new users until 2026-10-31—the loader returns the K3 window as documented, with no `exc = { "k2" = 262144 }`. The advisor can therefore allow roughly 4x too much context for Kimi K2 models.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:68

chunk_findings.detail: `local.cache_kind` is `s = "documented"` with `v = "automatic"`, but the note says vLLM automatic prefix caching applies “once enabled” and that `enable_prefix_caching=True` enables it. Given a vLLM endpoint started without APC enabled, the row still returns `cache_kind.v = "automatic"` with status `documented`, so the advisor can assume prefix caching exists when it does not. The conditional is only in the human-readable note; the machine-readable fact is unconditional.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:84

chunk_findings.detail: The `[harness.cursor]` row still records the dated observation “compaction threshold not found (looked 2026-10-23); only a maxMode switch” as a free-text top-level `note` rather than as a provenance-bearing fact. The file’s own contract requires facts to be `{v, s, src, d, note?}` and says a row with no facts is an explicit unknown; a known absence for `window_knob` should be represented as `window_knob = { s = "none", src = "window-note", d = "2026-10-23", note = ... }`, as done for `copilot` and `aider`. Given `facts("cursor")`, the advisor sees no `window_knob` and must treat Cursor as unknown, and given `[context].facts_max_age_days` smaller than the age of the 2026-10-23 observation, stale-age checking will not flag this note, unlike the equivalent dated `copilot.window_knob` fact. This is the same untriaged previous finding #5 and remains unfixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_harnesses.toml:[harness.cursor]

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s acceptance criterion is “probe record per UNVERIFIED line,” and its intent says to “run and record the probes.” This file still records no executed probes: line 5 says “No probe below is `verified`,” and line 31 explicitly lists live execution as “Not done, on purpose.” For example, the PostCompact-summary row is marked only “documented,” so an acceptance check requiring an executed probe record (or a logged live payload) fails for every UNVERIFIED line, and the advisor would be relying on vendor-page inference rather than the required live probe.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:31

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s acceptance criterion requires a probe record for each UNVERIFIED line in research section 11 (hooks that reach subagents, PostCompact summary fields, Kimi cache behavior, and the compaction-cold cache write), and the intent explicitly says to “run and record” those live probes. The added probe document still carries the live-execution statement “Not done, on purpose” (shown in the manifest for this file), so the required executed-probe records are absent. For example, a reader who needs to know whether a hook payload reaches subagents or whether PostCompact supplies a summary still has no probe record for those lines, so the acceptance requirement is not satisfied.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md

data.body:
Fixes bug B5612a09e73: The standards-gate helper `python -m ddflow.services.roborev_branch`, run with no arguments from a worktree as the gate text prescribes, uses the literal '--local' as base and records unavailable ('no merge-base of --local and HEAD'). It only works with --base main --repo . Probe: run it in any item worktree. Found on CC-inventory.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B5612a09e73 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B5612a09e73 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B5612a09e73: roborev_branch without --base reports unavailable: no merge-base of '--local' and HEAD

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` still does not robustly return problems for malformed but parseable shipped TOML; it can raise instead. For `{"context_families.toml": {"family": []}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}}`, `_shape_problems` correctly reports that `family` is not a table, but execution then reaches `unknown = family_row(data, UNKNOWN)`, whose `rows.get` call is made on the list `[]` and raises `AttributeError`. The same assumption appears in `_fact_problems`: `f.get("src") not in doc.get("sources", {})` assumes `sources` is a mapping and `src` is hashable, so a fact with `src = ["x"]` raises `TypeError`, while `sources = ["x"]` lets a fact with `src = "x"` pass validation even though `[sources]` is not a table. These malformed-data cases should be returned as validation problems, not crash or silently pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: The Gemini row encodes `min_tokens = { v = 2048, s = "documented", ... note = "2048-4096 depending on model" }` with no `exc` or `only`. The file’s own contract says model-dependent differences belong in `exc`/`only`; a note is not machine-readable. Given a Gemini model whose actual cache-write minimum is 4096 — the note asserts such models exist — the loader still returns `2048` as a documented family fact. An advisor using that value can attempt a 2048-token cache write that is below the provider minimum, causing the write to fail or not be cached.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:family.gemini.min_tokens

chunk_findings.detail: `family.glm.min_tokens` is a family-wide documented fact (`v = 512`, `s = "documented"`), but its note says the value is for “Zhipu-deployed GLM on Model Studio only,” and the adjacent `cache_kind` note says the direct Zhipu API was not read. Given a model name that resolves to `family.glm` but is served by the direct Zhipu API, e.g. `glm-4-plus`, the loader returns `512` as a documented model fact even though the source did not document that endpoint. If the direct API’s minimum differs, the advisor uses the wrong minimum; the provider/deployment restriction is only in prose and has no machine-readable scope.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:family.glm.min_tokens

chunk_findings.detail: The `family.qwen` row marks `cache_kind`, `ttl`, `read_mult`, `write_mult`, and `min_tokens` as documented family-wide facts, while the notes say they apply via Alibaba Model Studio only and/or only in explicit mode, with implicit mode having different values (`create 1.0x`, `hit ~0.2x`, TTL indeterminate). Given a Qwen model served outside Model Studio, or a Model Studio Qwen model using implicit caching, the loader still returns `cache_kind = "explicit"`, `ttl = ["5m"]`, `read_mult = 0.1`, `write_mult = 1.25`, and `min_tokens = 1024` as documented. The advisor can then attempt explicit breakpoints and a 5-minute TTL, or price cache writes at 1.25x, on an endpoint where explicit caching is unavailable or where implicit create cost is 1.0x.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:family.qwen

chunk_findings.detail: Row 7 records “`additionalContext` is not accepted on PreCompact” with status `documented`, but the cited source is the hooks page from row 1, which (per the change’s own triage) only fails to list `additionalContext` for PreCompact. Absence from a list of accepted fields does not prove the field is rejected. Given a PreCompact hook that returns `additionalContext`, the runtime could still accept it, but this document tells the advisor the path is documented as unavailable. The claim should be “not listed”/open, not a documented negative.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:18

chunk_findings.detail: Row 5 states “No prompt-cache key appears in the config reference” while the source column says the source was only the first 100 K characters of the Codex config reference, and the next step is to read the rest of the page. If the full reference contains a prompt-cache key after the first 100 K characters, this negative fact is false; the row’s own source admits it did not see the whole reference. The absence should be `open`/`unverified` until the full page or source is checked.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:16

data.reason: the review was terminated by SIGTERM before a reviewer finished: nothing was reviewed, which is not a pass

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` is documented to return problems, but several membership tests assume a table/string and are not type- or hash-checked. `_fact_problems` does `f.get("src") not in doc.get("sources", {})` while `_field_problems` never validates `src` or `[sources]`. Given parseable TOML with a normal `[sources]` table and one fact whose `src = ["a"]`, `_shape_problems` accepts the row shape and `_fact_problems` evaluates `["a"] not in {"a": {}}`, raising `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` instead of returning a source problem. Given `sources = "abc"` and `src = "b"`, the same line treats `"b" in "abc"` as a valid source, so `validate` can return no problem even though there is no `[sources]` key. The same unguarded `in` remains in `validate`: `UNKNOWN not in ... .get("family", {})` raises for `family = 1`, and `hid not in rows` raises for `harness = 1` when `harness_ids=["h"]`. The earlier `family_row` `isinstance` check does not answer these paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: `facts()` is documented as returning every fact of one parsed file, but it returns facts from only one table: it chooses `family` whenever the key exists, otherwise `harness`. `_fact_problems` and `stale` depend on this. Given `context_harnesses.toml` parsed as `{"family": {}, "harness": {"h": {"x": {"s": "bogus", "v": 1, "src": "a", "d": "2024-01-01"}}}, "sources": {"a": {}}}` (an accidental empty `[family]` table) and a families file with `family.unknown = {}`, `validate` returns `[]` and `stale` returns `[]`: `_shape_problems` accepts the empty `[family]` table and the harness fact’s shape, but `facts()` never yields the harness fact, so its invalid status/date/value rules are silently skipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:facts

chunk_findings.detail: The inline table for `[family.qwen] cache_kind` is opened with `{` but never closed: the line ends with `... only"` and no trailing `}`. The `[family.glm] cache_kind` table at line 82 has the same missing closing brace. TOML inline tables must be terminated on the same line, so `load()`/`tomllib` raises a TOML decode error at line 75 (and would still fail at line 82 after that fix); the shipped table is not parseable, so `load`/doctor/tests such as `test_shipped_tables_are_well_formed` cannot read the facts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:75

chunk_findings.detail: The Qwen rows at lines 75-79 are marked as documented family-wide facts while their notes restrict them to Model Studio explicit mode and explicitly say implicit mode differs. Given a Qwen model using implicit caching, `facts` still returns `cache_kind = "explicit"`, `ttl = ["5m"]`, `read_mult = 0.1`, and `write_mult = 1.25`; the note says implicit mode has create `1.0x`, hit `~0.2x`, and an indeterminate TTL. The advisor will therefore price cache writes/hits and TTL using explicit-mode numbers for an implicit-mode request. The notes are not machine-readable, and there is no `only`/mode scoping or left-out representation, so the family-wide-fact defect remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:76

chunk_findings.detail: `family.claude.compaction_kind = "client_summary"` is sourced from `claude-hooks` and its note says “Claude Code summarises the conversation.” The file’s own scope says a family row describes the vendor’s own API and that harness capabilities live in `context_harnesses.toml`. For an Anthropic API client that is not Claude Code, the loader still returns `client_summary` as a model-family fact, causing the advisor to assume client-side summarisation and PreCompact/PostCompact hook behavior where that is harness behavior, not a vendor API fact.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:43

chunk_findings.detail: The fact records `GOOSE_CACHE_TTL` as an unconditional `s = "documented"` capability, but its own note says it is “Anthropic only” and that “headless runs always 5m”. The fact contract supports machine-readable `exc`/`only` for exactly this kind of applicability restriction; a note is not machine-readable. Given a Goose harness using a non-Anthropic provider, or a headless run, `facts("goose")["ttl_env"]` still returns `GOOSE_CACHE_TTL` as documented, so an advisor can set that environment variable expecting prompt-cache TTL control even though the source says it does not apply.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_harnesses.toml:52 harness.goose.ttl_env

chunk_findings.detail: The fact records `compaction.reserved` as a documented window knob, but the note says “a model without limit.context is never auto-compacted”. That is a model-dependent exception to the usefulness of the knob, and it is encoded only in prose. Given a model without `limit.context`, the loader still returns `window_knob` as available; an advisor can recommend setting `compaction.reserved` to control auto-compaction, but per the source that model will never auto-compact regardless of the reserved-token setting. The condition belongs in `exc`/`only`, not just in `note`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_harnesses.toml:60 harness.opencode.window_knob

chunk_findings.detail: The fact value is a closed list of events, while the note says PreCompact and PostCompact are merely “not listed there” for `additionalContext`, not explicitly denied. Given a PreCompact hook that returns `additionalContext`, `facts("claude")["context_events"]` omits `PreCompact`, so an advisor treating the documented list as the supported event set will mark that path unavailable even though the source only records absence from the page, not rejection. The uncertainty should be encoded as an exception or unverified state, not as an omission from a machine-readable documented list.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_harnesses.toml:22 harness.claude.context_events

chunk_findings.detail: Row 5 states “No prompt-cache key appears in the config reference” while its source column admits it only read the first 100 K characters of the Codex config reference. That makes the answer an unsupported global negative: if any prompt-cache key exists after the first 100 K characters, an advisor consuming this research as a documented absence will wrongly conclude Codex exposes no prompt-cache configuration and may choose a different caching strategy. The row’s own next step (“read the rest of the page”) confirms the full reference has not been checked, so the negative fact should be scoped to the portion read or marked open/unverified until the rest is read.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:16

chunk_findings.detail: `facts()` chooses only one table per parsed document (`family` if present, otherwise `harness`), so facts under the other table are never seen by `_fact_problems` or `stale`. For example, pass to `validate()` a families document containing both `family.unknown = {}` and `harness.foo.max_context = {v=1, s="bogus", src="x", d="2026-01-01"}`. `_shape_problems()` explicitly inspects both `family` and `harness` tables, but `_fact_problems()` calls `facts(doc)`, which selects `family`, so the invalid status `"bogus"` is not reported. If a single file is not allowed to contain both tables, `validate()` also fails to report that malformed shape.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:facts

chunk_findings.detail: `validate()` performs membership checks directly on values that may not be mappings. Given a families document with `sources = "x"` and a fact whose `src = "x"`, the source check `f.get("src") not in doc.get("sources", {})` becomes `'x' not in "x"`, which is false, so an invalid scalar `sources` value is accepted as provenance; `sources = ["x"]` behaves the same. Given `sources = 5` (or a fact with `src = ["x"]` while `sources` is a table), the same line raises `TypeError` instead of returning a validation problem. The same unguarded membership pattern is used for `harness` rows and the `family` table, so malformed values such as `harness = 5` with `harness_ids=["foo"]` or `family = 5` can crash `validate()` rather than report malformed data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: `[family.claude].compaction_kind` is stored as a model-family fact but its source is `claude-hooks` and its note explicitly describes Claude Code (“Claude Code summarises the conversation; PreCompact/PostCompact hooks exist”). The file’s own header says family rows describe the vendor’s own API and that harness capabilities live in `context_harnesses.toml` (lines 15–16, 20). Given a direct Anthropic API model with no Claude Code harness, a loader reading family facts returns `compaction_kind = client_summary` as a documented model-family fact, because a harness has hooks. That is the wrong fact for the model family and can cause the advisor to assume client-side summary compaction for every Claude-family model.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:43

chunk_findings.detail: `[family.qwen]` stores explicit-mode Model Studio facts as unconditional family facts. The note on line 75 says the facts apply “via Alibaba Model Studio only” and describes both “explicit cache_control … or implicit …”; lines 76–79 further note that the TTL/read/write values are explicit-mode only, while implicit mode has create 1.0, hit ~0.2, and indeterminate TTL. The schema has no mode qualifier, so for a Qwen model using the documented implicit mode, `facts` returns `cache_kind=explicit`, `ttl=["5m"]`, `read_mult=0.1`, and `write_mult=1.25`, which are wrong for implicit mode. These facts should be scoped, left out, or marked unverified rather than documented as family facts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:75

chunk_findings.detail: Row 5 says “No prompt-cache key appears in the config reference,” but the source for that row is explicitly only the first 100 K characters of the page, and the next step is “read the rest of the page.” That records a negative as if it were documented from a partial read. If the Codex config reference contains a prompt-cache key after the fetched prefix, a reader or table relying on this line will treat the option as absent/open incorrectly; the evidence supports only “not found in the first 100 K characters,” not “no prompt-cache key appears.”
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:16

chunk_findings.detail: `test_old_facts_make_doctor_note_them` hard-codes that exactly one stale note exists at `date(2027, 2, 1)`. That date is 95 days after the test’s “not stale” date `date(2026, 10, 29)`, so with `max_age=90` every fact dated on or before 2026-10-29 is stale. The shipped loader contains multiple dated facts (e.g. `family.claude.read_mult`, `family.claude.window`, `family.claude.min_tokens`, `family.openai.write_mult`, `family.deepseek.read_mult`, `family.kimi.window`, plus harness facts), so `CF.stale` should return multiple entries. If `CF.doctor_notes` returns one note per stale fact, `len(notes) == 1` fails; if it aggregates all stale facts into one note, the assertion no longer tests the intended “one old fact” behavior and hides the multiple stale facts.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_families.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: `test_shipped_tables_are_well_formed` and `test_every_harness_id_has_a_row` require a context row for every harness id discovered under `paths.package_dir() / "harnesses"`. The stated triage says Cursor/Windsurf are intentionally left out rather than documented as none. If those harness definitions are present (as implied by the triage), their ids are in `IDS`, the context table omits them, and `CF.validate` reports missing rows (as demonstrated by `test_a_missing_harness_row_is_reported`), so `validate(...) == []` and the coverage assertion fail. The test enforces the opposite of the triaged behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_families.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` still does not robustly return problems for malformed but parseable shipped TOML; it can raise instead. For `{"context_families.toml": {"family": []}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}}`, `_shape_problems` correctly reports that `family` is not a table, but execution then reaches `unknown = family_row(data, UNKNOWN)`, whose `rows.get` call is made on the list `[]` and raises `AttributeError`. The same assumption appears in `_fact_problems`: `f.get("src") not in doc.get("sources", {})` assumes `sources` is a mapping and `src` is hashable, so a fact with `src = ["x"]` raises `TypeError`, while `sources = ["x"]` lets a fact with `src = "x"` pass validation even though `[sources]` is not a table. These malformed-data cases should be returned as validation problems, not crash or silently pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: The Gemini row encodes `min_tokens = { v = 2048, s = "documented", ... note = "2048-4096 depending on model" }` with no `exc` or `only`. The file’s own contract says model-dependent differences belong in `exc`/`only`; a note is not machine-readable. Given a Gemini model whose actual cache-write minimum is 4096 — the note asserts such models exist — the loader still returns `2048` as a documented family fact. An advisor using that value can attempt a 2048-token cache write that is below the provider minimum, causing the write to fail or not be cached.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:family.gemini.min_tokens

chunk_findings.detail: `family.glm.min_tokens` is a family-wide documented fact (`v = 512`, `s = "documented"`), but its note says the value is for “Zhipu-deployed GLM on Model Studio only,” and the adjacent `cache_kind` note says the direct Zhipu API was not read. Given a model name that resolves to `family.glm` but is served by the direct Zhipu API, e.g. `glm-4-plus`, the loader returns `512` as a documented model fact even though the source did not document that endpoint. If the direct API’s minimum differs, the advisor uses the wrong minimum; the provider/deployment restriction is only in prose and has no machine-readable scope.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:family.glm.min_tokens

chunk_findings.detail: The `family.qwen` row marks `cache_kind`, `ttl`, `read_mult`, `write_mult`, and `min_tokens` as documented family-wide facts, while the notes say they apply via Alibaba Model Studio only and/or only in explicit mode, with implicit mode having different values (`create 1.0x`, `hit ~0.2x`, TTL indeterminate). Given a Qwen model served outside Model Studio, or a Model Studio Qwen model using implicit caching, the loader still returns `cache_kind = "explicit"`, `ttl = ["5m"]`, `read_mult = 0.1`, `write_mult = 1.25`, and `min_tokens = 1024` as documented. The advisor can then attempt explicit breakpoints and a 5-minute TTL, or price cache writes at 1.25x, on an endpoint where explicit caching is unavailable or where implicit create cost is 1.0x.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:family.qwen

chunk_findings.detail: Row 7 records “`additionalContext` is not accepted on PreCompact” with status `documented`, but the cited source is the hooks page from row 1, which (per the change’s own triage) only fails to list `additionalContext` for PreCompact. Absence from a list of accepted fields does not prove the field is rejected. Given a PreCompact hook that returns `additionalContext`, the runtime could still accept it, but this document tells the advisor the path is documented as unavailable. The claim should be “not listed”/open, not a documented negative.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:18

chunk_findings.detail: Row 5 states “No prompt-cache key appears in the config reference” while the source column says the source was only the first 100 K characters of the Codex config reference, and the next step is to read the rest of the page. If the full reference contains a prompt-cache key after the first 100 K characters, this negative fact is false; the row’s own source admits it did not see the whole reference. The absence should be `open`/`unverified` until the full page or source is checked.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:16

chunk_findings.detail: The new unknown-row guard still evaluates `UNKNOWN not in data["context_families.toml"].get("family", {})` before ensuring that the value is a mapping. Given malformed but parseable data such as `{"context_families.toml": {"family": 5}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}}`, `family_row` returns `{}` because `rows` is not a dict, then `UNKNOWN not in 5` raises `TypeError`. Thus `validate` crashes instead of returning the shape problem it is supposed to report; the previous robustness issue remains for scalar/non-iterable `family` values.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:validate

chunk_findings.detail: The sources type check rejects an empty table as if it were not a table. After `sources = doc.get("sources", {})` is coerced to `{}` for non-dicts, `if "sources" in doc and not sources` is also true when the original value was `{}`. For a parseable file/doc like `{"sources": {}}` with no facts, `_fact_problems` returns `"...: sources is not a table"`, although an empty `[sources]` table is a table and the later source-membership check already handles an empty source table correctly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:_fact_problems

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that `facts()` reads both tables, but the family table in `doc` contains only `{"unknown": {}}`, i.e. zero facts. Therefore the assertion `len(CF.facts(doc)) == 1` is satisfied even by a regression where `facts()` reads only the `harness` table and ignores `family`; the test passes without proving that family facts are loaded. To guard the stated `facts() reads both tables` fix, the test needs at least one fact under `family` and must assert that it is returned.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_families.py:test_facts_of_both_tables_are_validated_and_sources_must_be_a_table

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` reports malformed table shapes but then crashes before returning those problems when the malformed value is non-iterable. For example, given `{"context_families.toml": {"family": 1}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}}`, `_shape_problems` correctly appends `context_families.toml: family is not a table`, but the later unknown-row check executes `"unknown" not in data["context_families.toml"].get("family", {})`, i.e. `"unknown" not in 1`, raising `TypeError`. The same pattern exists for `harness`: with `harness = 1` and a non-empty `harness_ids`, `hid not in rows` raises `TypeError` instead of returning the shape problem. A validator should guard these membership tests and return the problems.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py: validate

chunk_findings.detail: An explicit empty `[sources]` table is treated as a malformed table. The code does `sources = doc.get("sources", {})`, then `if "sources" in doc and not sources: problems.append("sources is not a table")`, so a well-formed parsed TOML value `{"sources": {}}` produces `sources is not a table` even though it is a table. Meanwhile, a file with no facts and no `sources` key at all passes. Thus adding an explicit empty sources table makes otherwise valid data fail, while omitting sources entirely does not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py: _fact_problems

chunk_findings.detail: The file’s stated scope says a family row describes the vendor’s own API and that third-party routes such as Model Studio belong in DRV-model-catalog. The GLM row explicitly says its facts were seen only for “Zhipu-deployed GLM on Model Studio” and that “the direct Zhipu API was not read.” Given a direct Zhipu model name such as `glm-4.6`, the loader can match `family.glm` and obtain `cache_kind` and `min_tokens` entries whose provenance is a third-party route, not the vendor API. If the unverified `v` is surfaced as a lead, or if any consumer treats the family row as vendor-API data, it will apply Model Studio cache behavior to the direct Zhipu API, violating the file’s own scope.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:[family.glm]

chunk_findings.detail: The same scope says routes such as local servers belong in DRV-model-catalog, not in family rows. The `[REDACTED:host]` row is explicitly about self-hosted endpoints and server flags (“caching belongs to the SERVER and its flags, not to the model”), and its only source is vLLM APC. Given a local llama.cpp or Ollama endpoint, the table still exposes `cache_kind = "automatic"` sourced from vLLM; this route/server fact should not be encoded as a model-family fact and can cause reports or advisors to assume automatic caching for local endpoints whose server does not enable it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:[[REDACTED:host]]

chunk_findings.detail: The “Not done, on purpose” section says “prices in absolute terms: not read,” but the same file’s “Other facts read for the tables” section already records absolute DeepSeek prices (“per 1M tokens off-peak: flash hit $0.003, miss $0.15, output $0.6; pro hit $0.022, miss $0.66, output $1.98”). A reader or downstream tool relying on the “not done” claim will believe no absolute price data was collected, while the document actually contains it and contradicts its own scope statement.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:33

chunk_findings.detail: `test_old_facts_make_doctor_note_them` asserts `len(notes) == 1` after calling `CF.doctor_notes(90, date(2027, 2, 1))`, but `doctor_notes` returns notes for *all* stale facts. This encodes an accidental property of the currently shipped tables rather than testing the stale-note behavior. For example, if the shipped family table legitimately contains another documented fact dated `2026-10-23` (the same date already used in `test_a_malformed_or_misspelt_fact_is_not_silently_dropped`), then at `date(2027, 2, 1)` both that fact and `family.claude.ttl` are older than 90 days, so `doctor_notes` returns at least two notes and line 69 fails even though staleness detection is correct. The test should filter for the expected `family.claude.ttl` note or use synthetic data instead of asserting an exact count over shipped data.

chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_families.py:test_facts_of_both_tables_are_validated_and_sources_must_be_a_table

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed robustness fix still leaves the source-membership check able to raise on malformed but parseable TOML. `_fact_problems` tests `f.get("src") not in sources` where `sources` is a dict. If a fact table has a non-hashable `src` value, such as `src = []` or `src = {}`, the `in` test on a dict raises `TypeError` before any problem can be appended. For example, given `{"context_families.toml": {"family": {"claude": {"min_tokens": {"v": 1, "s": "documented", "src": []}}}, "sources": {"x": {}}}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}}`, `validate` should report an invalid/unknown source, but it raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. The new `sources = {}` coercion only handles a non-mapping `sources`; it does not make the left operand of `in` safe.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py:_fact_problems

chunk_findings.detail: `validate` reports malformed table shapes but then crashes before returning those problems when the malformed value is non-iterable. For example, given `{"context_families.toml": {"family": 1}, "context_harnesses.toml": {"harness": {}}}`, `_shape_problems` correctly appends `context_families.toml: family is not a table`, but the later unknown-row check executes `"unknown" not in data["context_families.toml"].get("family", {})`, i.e. `"unknown" not in 1`, raising `TypeError`. The same pattern exists for `harness`: with `harness = 1` and a non-empty `harness_ids`, `hid not in rows` raises `TypeError` instead of returning the shape problem. A validator should guard these membership tests and return the problems.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py: validate

chunk_findings.detail: An explicit empty `[sources]` table is treated as a malformed table. The code does `sources = doc.get("sources", {})`, then `if "sources" in doc and not sources: problems.append("sources is not a table")`, so a well-formed parsed TOML value `{"sources": {}}` produces `sources is not a table` even though it is a table. Meanwhile, a file with no facts and no `sources` key at all passes. Thus adding an explicit empty sources table makes otherwise valid data fail, while omitting sources entirely does not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/context_families.py: _fact_problems

chunk_findings.detail: The file’s stated scope says a family row describes the vendor’s own API and that third-party routes such as Model Studio belong in DRV-model-catalog. The GLM row explicitly says its facts were seen only for “Zhipu-deployed GLM on Model Studio” and that “the direct Zhipu API was not read.” Given a direct Zhipu model name such as `glm-4.6`, the loader can match `family.glm` and obtain `cache_kind` and `min_tokens` entries whose provenance is a third-party route, not the vendor API. If the unverified `v` is surfaced as a lead, or if any consumer treats the family row as vendor-API data, it will apply Model Studio cache behavior to the direct Zhipu API, violating the file’s own scope.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:[family.glm]

chunk_findings.detail: The same scope says routes such as local servers belong in DRV-model-catalog, not in family rows. The `[REDACTED:host]` row is explicitly about self-hosted endpoints and server flags (“caching belongs to the SERVER and its flags, not to the model”), and its only source is vLLM APC. Given a local llama.cpp or Ollama endpoint, the table still exposes `cache_kind = "automatic"` sourced from vLLM; this route/server fact should not be encoded as a model-family fact and can cause reports or advisors to assume automatic caching for local endpoints whose server does not enable it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/context_families.toml:[[REDACTED:host]]

chunk_findings.detail: The “Not done, on purpose” section says “prices in absolute terms: not read,” but the same file’s “Other facts read for the tables” section already records absolute DeepSeek prices (“per 1M tokens off-peak: flash hit $0.003, miss $0.15, output $0.6; pro hit $0.022, miss $0.66, output $1.98”). A reader or downstream tool relying on the “not done” claim will believe no absolute price data was collected, while the document actually contains it and contradicts its own scope statement.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/context-probes.md:33

chunk_findings.detail: `test_old_facts_make_doctor_note_them` asserts `len(notes) == 1` after calling `CF.doctor_notes(90, date(2027, 2, 1))`, but `doctor_notes` returns notes for *all* stale facts. This encodes an accidental property of the currently shipped tables rather than testing the stale-note behavior. For example, if the shipped family table legitimately contains another documented fact dated `2026-10-23` (the same date already used in `test_a_malformed_or_misspelt_fact_is_not_silently_dropped`), then at `date(2027, 2, 1)` both that fact and `family.claude.ttl` are older than 90 days, so `doctor_notes` returns at least two notes and line 69 fails even though staleness detection is correct. The test should filter for the expected `family.claude.ttl` note or use synthetic data instead of asserting an exact count over shipped data.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_context_families.py:69
